proof:
# Exact endpoint budgets can obstruct flat strictification

This note gives a local obstruction to replacing the special symmetry or
common-fraction identities by a generic claim that an arbitrary finite
list of cap budgets can be preserved exactly during strictification.
It is not a counterexample to OC or to a budget-nonincreasing variation.

Fix d>=1, an integer m>=3, and a full-dimensional convex body K in R^d,
with V=|K|. Let C=[0,m-1] times K. Its m actual integer fibers all equal K.
Choose a nonzero u, write l=min_K u.x and r=max_K u.x, and set

    b=l-1,     A=r-l+3.

The nonvertical ambient halfspaces

    H_0={u.x-Az>=b},
    H_1={u.x+A(z-(m-1))>=b}

contain exactly the entire first and last integer fibers, respectively.
Indeed the retained endpoint has margin at least 1, while every unwanted
fiber has margin at most (r-l)-A+1=-2. This full/empty trace pattern
persists in a neighborhood of the finite fiber array and both halfspaces,
including independent small movements of their normals and thresholds.

Suppose an actual nearby convex fiber array J_0,...,J_(m-1) and nearby
caps H'_0,H'_1 preserve total mass and these two budgets exactly:

    sum_j |J_j|=mV,     mu_J(H'_0)=mu_J(H'_1)=V.              (1)

The stable trace pattern gives |J_0|=|J_(m-1)|=V. Actual convexity gives

    (1-j/(m-1))J_0 + (j/(m-1))J_(m-1) subset J_j.

By Brunn-Minkowski the set on the left has volume at least V. Thus every
|J_j|>=V. The total equality in (1) forces |J_j|=V for every j and equality
of each displayed inclusion. To justify equality as sets, a proper
inclusion of full-dimensional compact convex bodies has strictly larger
volume: separating an outside point from the smaller compact set and
joining it to an interior ball of the smaller set produces a positive-
volume portion outside. Therefore

    J_j=(1-j/(m-1))J_0 + (j/(m-1))J_(m-1)                  (2)

for every interior index. In particular every support-function gap of
this endpoint representation is zero. The array has no open neighborhood
of independently perturbable fibers with actual convex compatibility.
For example, a small translation of J_0 alone in direction v violates
(2) at j=1 in a direction u with u.v>0 when all other fibers are fixed.

This proof needs only the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, not its equality
classification. If one additionally uses its standard positive-volume
equality case, (2) says all fibers are translates of a common body along
an affine center path, because the equal-volume endpoints must be
translates. That classification is not needed for the obstruction.

The two isolated endpoint budgets are each V, and hence can be made an
arbitrarily small fraction 1/m of the total. In particular both lie below
Gamma_d M/2 once m>2/Gamma_d. Their small size does not remove the exact
flatness obstruction. They do not form a cover of the entire mixed source,
so no below-OC covering family is constructed here.

If inequalities rather than equalities are allowed for the two budgets,
this argument no longer applies: shrinking both endpoints and expanding
interior fibers may preserve the total and lower both endpoint caps.
Conversely, adding both complementary halfspaces to the finite list
forces exactness from nonincrease and fixed total, since every opposite
pair partitions the actual source with null boundary. Those complementary
caps have large budgets; this strengthened obstruction still makes no
claim about a cover consisting only of small caps.

The result precisely rules out universal EXACT preservation of an
arbitrary finite cap list as a method for obtaining independent-fiber
compatibility. Special flat families and a general nonincrease theorem
remain logically different mechanisms.
